How to Read This Dashboard
A quick orientation for anyone opening this file for the first time.

WHAT THIS FILE IS

This is a single, self-contained page with three tabs. Each tab embeds a separate dashboard that was generated directly from one of the source workbooks — nothing on this page is typed in by hand. If a workbook is refreshed and re-uploaded through that tab's "Update" button, the tab's charts and tables recalculate in your browser and the new figures are saved back into this same HTML file, so the update travels with it. Sample figures may be present until each tab is connected to its live source.

THE THREE TABS

TabSource workbookWhat it shows
Enterprise Risk Assessment Enterprise Risk Assessment Register Operational risks (threats) and opportunities: inherent vs. residual score and priority, how many threats moved to a lower priority after controls, risk reduction, exposure by department before and after controls, the GRC action plan urgency, risk response before and after controls (and opportunity priority before and after action), an inherent likelihood × impact heat map, whether reviews are happening on cycle, treatment progress, open exposure by risk owner, register data-quality gaps, and the threats with the highest residual score.
Departmental Baseline Questionnaire Departmental Baseline & Compliance MASTER Compliance score by department and by control domain, the response mix across all questions answered (Y / P / N / N-A), open corrective actions, and key issues each department has raised in its own words.
GRC Progress Update GRC Progress Update workbook A rollup of programme progress: milestones completed vs. pending and the overall status of the GRC rollout.

READING THE COLOR CODES

High / N Medium / P Low / Y

Red/high tags mark unacceptable risk scores or an "N" (not in place) questionnaire answer — these drive the highest-priority corrective actions. Amber/medium tags mark elevated-but-manageable risk or a "P" (partial) answer. Green/low tags mark risk within tolerance or a "Y" (fully in place) answer. The small dot next to each tab name ( ready vs. pending) shows at a glance whether that tab's source data has been connected.

KEEPING DATA CURRENT

Each tab has its own "Update" button for uploading a refreshed copy of its source workbook. Refreshing recalculates that tab only; the other two are untouched. The save indicator in the top-right corner (next to the title) shows whether the most recent refresh has been written into this HTML file yet, or is currently only saved in this browser — use "Save to file" there to make a refresh permanent and shareable.

GOING DEEPER

This page is deliberately a summary. For the exact formula behind any individual figure — which workbook column it traces back to and how it is calculated — open that source workbook directly and look for its own Dashboard Guide tab, which documents every KPI, chart, and table field by field.

CLICKING A FIGURE

On all three tabs, clicking any number, bar, donut slice, grid cell or table row opens the matching records underneath the chart. Each record shows its Excel row number on the source sheet, so it can be found directly in the workbook. The list can be searched and downloaded as CSV.

Sample data shown for layout purposes — connect each section to its live source when ready.
